movie.title: Black Phone 2
movie.overview: Four years after defeating The Grabber, Finney Blake is struggling with life after captivity. When his younger sister Gwen begins receiving calls in her dreams from the Black Phone and seeing disturbing visions of three boys being stalked at a winter camp, the siblings become determined to solve the mystery and confront a killer who has grown more powerful in death and more significant to them than either could imagine.

reviews.author: MovieGuys
reviews.content:
As far as improbable sequels go, "Black Phone 2" isn't too bad. 

Revive a deceased bad guy you would have thought was done with and craft a tale that feels somewhat like the first film, blended with an almost "Nightmare on Elm Street" premise. 

I have to say these elements combined with a dash of nostalgia from the 80's works, quite well. Sure its not A grade horror but its still creative, creepy and above all, entertaining. 

In summary, a not unfamiliar but still well crafted tale of revenge from beyond the grave. Worth a look.

reviews.author: tmdb97554867
reviews.content:
**One of the best horror sequels that will go down as an instant classic in a couple of years**

I already feel like this film doesn't get enough praise for blending multiple horror franchises together, but still delivering something brand new that fits in the same world as the original film. It takes the classic camp setting but sets it in a blizzard (Friday The 13th meets The Shining). It explores dreams, the spiritual realm and the afterlife (A Nightmare On Elm Street meets Insidious meets Poltergeist). The story and tone are also much more in line with modern storytelling (Terrifier meets Hereditary). The soundtrack is also incredibly retro with a hint of child-like wonder. (Sinister meets Five Nights At Freddy's). I generally cannot express how well it all blends together to deliver a realistic portrayal of a spirit that escaped from hell. If you think The Grabber is just a Freddy Krueger rip-off, then you completely missed the point of the film.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: This is quite a decent icy thriller, but is hasn’t anywhere near the claustrophobic intensity of the first film from 2021. It is still Mason Thames who portrays the now seventeen year old “Finn”, convinced that he seen the last of the “Grabber” but still having nightmares about a phone ringing. To add to his sleeplessness, his sister “Gwen” (also still Madeleine McGraw) is having some fairly torturous nightmares that, coupled with some sleep-walking, are unsettling both of them. Determined to find out what is causing these traumas, they hook up with her fellow Duran Duran fan “Ernesto” (Miguel Mora) and head to the very Christian fellowship camp where their mum was a counsellor. They arrive just as the mother of all blizzards sets in, and so up to their elbows in snow and ice they have to piece together just what happened to half a dozen children reported killed at the place but never found, and establish whether or not the dastardly “Grabber” is still something to be reckoned with. The cold and frosty environment and half decent efforts from Thames and McGraw do help to keep this mystery rolling along, but despite some curious and menacing flashbacks that fill us in with what did and might happen, the story here just isn’t very solid or original. It takes far too long to get going, and the denouement - though quite action-packed, is all just too rushed and disappointing. I did quite like the barbed remarks aimed at the god-fearing/adoring “Barb” (Maev Beaty) and it’s all perfectly watchable, but it could easily lose twenty minutes to condense the plot and get us to the snowy sharp-end a bit more swiftly. Worth a watch, but not as good.

reviews.author: Dean
reviews.content: It was just okay. First one was better. I understand that horror movies aren't realistic usually, but this one was way too much unrealistic unlike first part.

reviews.author: Alunauwie
reviews.content:
Black Phone (2025) shifts its horror focus from confinement to lingering trauma, revealing that Finn’s past terror never truly faded with time. As supernatural threats blur with internal fears, the film explores grief, denial, and inherited wounds rather than pure physical danger. While solid in character development and atmosphere, its reduced focus on the phone itself and unanswered questions leave the story feeling more like a bridge than a full reckoning.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Four years after surviving The Grabber, Finney Blake and his sister Gwen must decipher supernatural dream calls to stop a resurrected killer stalking a winter camp.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Four years after surviving his traumatic abduction, Finney Blake continues to struggle with the psychological aftermath of defeating The Grabber. When his younger sister Gwen begins experiencing supernatural dream calls from the black phone, she receives visions of boys being hunted at a winter camp. Realizing the supernatural threat is far from over, the siblings team up to unravel the mystery. Together, they must confront a terrifying killer who has returned from beyond the grave with newfound, personal power.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Set four years after Finney Blake successfully escaped and defeated his kidnapper, life remains difficult for the traumatized survivor. While Finney attempts to navigate his post-captivity life, his sister Gwen discovers that her psychic abilities are taking a darker, more unsettling turn. Gwen begins receiving mysterious phone calls in her dreams originating from the iconic black phone, accompanied by terrifying visions. These visions reveal three young boys being relentlessly stalked at a remote winter camp by an ominous entity. Recognizing that the supernatural calls are a dire warning, Gwen convinces Finney that they must take action to prevent another tragedy. As they investigate the camp and its dark connection to their past, they discover that the killer's spirit has transcended death. This resurrected force is not only stronger and more vengeful, but it also shares a deeply personal link to the Blake family. Finney and Gwen must rally their courage and face their deepest fears to permanently destroy an entity that threatens to consume them both.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Four years after surviving his harrowing ordeal at the hands of The Grabber, Finney Blake struggles to reintegrate into normal life while coping with post-traumatic stress. Meanwhile, his sister Gwen's psychic powers resurface through ominous dream calls from the uncanny black phone, projecting visions of three young boys in danger at a winter camp. Driven by a desperate need to save innocent lives and uncover the truth, the siblings embark on a perilous journey that unearths dark secrets connecting the killer to their own family history, leading to an ultimate confrontation with a powerful supernatural threat.

faq.answer: Yes, Black Phone 2 is part of a film franchise. It serves as a direct sequel to the 2021 supernatural horror hit The Black Phone.

faq.answer: The dominant genre of Black Phone 2 is supernatural horror, combined with elements of mystery and thriller.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre of Black Phone 2?

faq.answer: The movie was directed by Scott Derrickson, who also directed the first film and co-wrote the sequel screenplay with C. Robert Cargill.
faq.question: Who directed Black Phone 2?

faq.answer: Key returning cast members include Mason Thames as Finney Blake, Madeleine McGraw as Gwen Blake, Jeremy Davies as Terrence Blake, and Ethan Hawke as The Grabber.
faq.question: Who are the main cast members returning for Black Phone 2?

faq.answer: Set four years after Finney escapes captivity, the plot follows Gwen as she receives dream calls on the Black Phone showing visions of three boys being stalked at a winter camp. Together, the siblings head to the camp to solve the mystery and face a now-supernatural Grabber.
faq.question: What is the main plot of Black Phone 2?

faq.answer: Yes, Ethan Hawke reprises his role as The Grabber, returning as a ghostly entity who has become even more powerful and malevolent in death.
faq.question: Does Ethan Hawke return as The Grabber in the sequel?

faq.answer: While the original 2021 film was adapted directly from Joe Hill's short story 'The Black Phone', the sequel features an original storyline co-conceived by Joe Hill and expanded by screenwriters Scott Derrickson and C. Robert Cargill.
